reviews.text: Fun

A small dev team has put a lot of love and passion into this game, and it shows. Savara could be described as "Hades meets Monster Hunter" : fight creatures of different sizes, collect their body parts and craft your weapons and armor. Do not expect it to be as fast as Hades, its combat is slower but still very interesting and satisfying. The game is mostly light-hearted and has a simple but fun story, with some great characters. I also had a lot of fun trying to find some easter eggs and references hidden throughout the game. In summary, I definitely recommend Savara, it is a great game with a lot of replayability and fun unique features.
If Hades and Monster Hunter had a love child, this would be it. Highly recommend!
挺好玩的，就是啃生肉有点费劲。玩了一把双刀和盾剑，双刀位移很好用，盾有格挡能加容错，打那种带灼烧地板的怪可以一直完美格挡丢技能，很好用。就是略微刮痧，一把打了五十五分钟。

Found the demo interesting so I gave it a shot, but the gameplay did get repetitive in the early game, and the unlocks for weapons and powers were underwhelming. The pros: its an interesting Monster Hunter style roguelike, with unique weapons and combo mechanics. The game is smooth, the combos are weighty enough, and each weapon is fun for different playstyles. The game has a pretty decent UI and animations and artwork are great. While playing i felt that this game was very inspired by really great parts of different roguelikes, and they took a lot of great concepts from those games and incorporated them here. However, ultimately there were some negatives. a lot of actions are tied to a stamina system including your basic and heavy attacks, which can make it a much more slower game. Swapping weapons triggers an attack while switching weapons, and restores some stamina. This game expects you be kiting the monster, using weapon swaps to restore stamina that is lost when dodging and attacking, but the systems make it just a waiting game to wait for openings before being able to do meaningful damage. This is just very boring unfortunately. Most runs were just me doing a 2 hit combo -> weapon swap attack -> two hit combo... on loop in order to circumvent stamina issues. There are powers and perks that help you reduce stamina costs, but nothing really beats the consistent DPS of the loop. Stack on top the fact that each weapon has a different damage type of 3 (blunt, slashing, etc.) but only 2 weapons can be equipped at a time. If you did not bring the right weapon damage type, a fight can easily drag on. Elites in normal rooms were especially draining to fight. They were absolute damage sponges, and if you were not able to get any good DPS powers in your pool, you will be spending a lot of the early game spending more time than it should to beat normal rooms. I felt like I spent a lot of time in rooms trying to pick off small targets, waiting out attacks, then striking a few times, and repeating waiting. After a few runs, this waiting game doesn't really change even with more damage, its just part of the pace of the game. It creates this odd feeling where you want to die faster in a run to get more upgrade rather than continuing because of how it will take per room. And at that point I realized I was not really enjoying my time in the early game if I was already getting annoyed that rooms took a while. Granted, as I unlocked more perks, I found opportunities to increase damage, but it felt really bad that early that I felt I had gotten the main combat loop down by my second run. Some weapons have very little incentive to do their heavy attack, even with heavy attack perks. The powers, though not entirely generic, only felt the most impactful when carrying one god's powers alone rather than mixing and matching. They did not feel like powers you could build around, just mild enhancements to your combo. Some had some cool scaling in the late game, but were not a highlight for me. I think it would have been more fun to craft temporary perks for your weapons at different spots in the game. The windup on some of the boss attacks also feel so delayed. there is a bonus for dodging perfectly, but I would constantly misjudge the timing on attacks. Even more infuriating was attacks that came out instantly after an indicator mixed in with attacks that take literal seconds of windup past the indicator. It felt inconsistent as a warning, and the best strat is just sprint away entirely from bosses rather than try to time dodges. I ended up just using the sword and shield equipped in two slots so I could weapon swap while shielding (invincible) basically giving me two outs to improper dodging. in terms of gear, the gear comes with a set bonus (usually something that increases based on how much of the armor set you are wearing) and a general equipment bonus, unlocked througb monster parts from killing. it was slightly interesting based on how armor interacted with certain equippables (one that gives bonus damage on low health might synergize with a trinket that drains your health and increases damage based on low health for example), but it was clear the final biome has the best armor and best set bonus. So the idea that the armor could lead to interesting combinations is a bit misleading when one set is just better than the others. The only time I considered mixing was just because I had no other resources to craft a full set. Weapons are similar where you need significant investment before their unique passive unlocks, and then even more upgrades to make that passive useful. If it was possible to smith between worlds, this might actually be a fun way to feel tangible change in strength, but unfortunately you can only smith after you die. So even if you get plenty of materials, you dont feel any meaningful strength outside of powers, so you dont really dynamically change as you continue in your run. Overall, I really wanted to enjoy this game, and it was a well polished and clean game, but ultimately not for me. Part of the grind of games like this has to keep my interest, but I unfortunately fell off from the stamina mechanics and early game slog. The enemies also repeat throughout biomes, so enemy variety felt a bit off as well. Bosses are essentially just larger versions of a basic monster with multiple attacks from other monsters you've seen throughout the biome. It all ended up being less satisfying than what I got in the demo. If I were to give advice for what I wish the game had, I hope they could tune down the HP on the elites by maybe 10-20% or make it so even if you dont match damage type for a monster you dont deal absolutely pitiful damage. The game is weird at forcing you to want to weapon switch as combos, but also punishing constant weapon swaps with the different damage types being strong on some enemies and weaker on others. It was not even really a matter of the game being difficult, just boring to have to spend so much time on one enemy doing the same loop.Bosses will enrage and basically be uninteractable except for very small windows between attacks, making it even more drawn out. If the devs make some changes to prevent the burnout in the early game, I might pick up again around another sale. If you felt you were concerned by anything the review, I'd say give the demo a shot, and see if you can understand where I am coming from for some of the points I made.

I was addicted to the game since demo, and it is a awesome game. But I feel like the Hades loop doesn't fit that well. Maybe a "Trophy Hunting" style with different small maps and roguelike elements would feel less repetitive and more intetional.

This game is basically "Early Access Hades". It's polished but it really lacks content, maybe there will be patch in the future? But now it's only straight-forward "hack & slash". The problem is that the fights feel really slow, but the most important part that sometimes your actions does not get registered by the game so you easily get hit. For example: you are in the mid of the combo and you want to stop action or you want to use another skill and game just ignores it and continues your combo and you of course get hit by the enemy. Game is fun at the start but without any actual story at becomes repetitive and boring - your only source of fun is to obtain achievements from the game that really hard for casual players like me. I didn't really like soundtrack - it is really basic and monotonous. I had to disable it and use mine instead. Pros: + game is polished, no real bugs seen + good art-design + ability to customize your character + interesting but sometimes hard to beat bosses and mobs + your build and your abilities really matter (so every chosen made makes your build better or worse) Cons: - too basic soundtrack - no real story, no real interaction between "champions" - slow fights without ability to cancel combo - too easy to unlock all boons (I know I've played 18 hours but I think it's still too easy) Overall: this game really NEEDS content and soundtrack. For now it's 6.5/10 from me.

Mashup of Monster Hunter and Hades is the best way to describe this game. The stages leading up to each act boss are all fun, powerup synergies are well thought out, and lead to some pretty interesting builds. The distinct weapons are fun to master too. The UI is super clean, and I really liked the challenge that stamina management with the weapon swapping presented. I've run through the game enough times now to unlock prestige mode, so I got some enjoyment playing this game. Unfortunately, I would not recommend getting into this game in it's current state Bosses are an effing mess, and feel incredibly unfair. Enemy bosses do insane amounts of damage, and healing is not only rare to find, but too difficult to use, especially during enrages. Enemy AoEs tend to stick around for an absurdly long time, and bosses tend to sit in their own AoE's when they're not charging around the screen. There's been a few times where bosses kill me as soon as I enter their room with an offscreen attack. Other times where bosses knock me down with one hit, and kill me with the 2nd before I have time to get up. Also, I can't count the number of times that I've gotten hit by offscreen attacks. Bosses just tend to charge around the stage, going offscreen and following up with ranged attacks, and then charging offscreen again when you close in. A single hit from a boss is roughly the same amount of damage as you can heal in one go, even with maxed out healing badges. The Wolf and Dragon bosses are particularly awful in this respect. Also, weapon and armor upgrades seem lackluster unless you fully max them out, and this takes hours and hours of runs to max even one weapon. I'm one of those people that will replay a game until I unlock all the items and max them out, but I plan on simply uninstalling this game now that I've beaten it a few times. The boss fights are just tedious and no fun. There's a probably a good game here, I really like the more tactical approach to this roguelike, but the way progress and boss difficulty are handled is holding it back from actually being good.

Game's promising, but it lacks an absurd amount of content, so much it feels like a very early access one. Were it to have twice everything it offers (armor sets, weapon sets, talents, badges, enemies, zones, powers, abilities, etc.) it would still lack content. Runs take a long time due to enemies being sponges and rooms taking a long time to clear. I do like the game a lot, visuals and the combination of Hades and Monster Hunter is great. It sure is promising, but there's not much to do with that price range to justify it.

[h1]一点点怪猎再加一点点哈迪斯[/h1] [h2] 推荐指数：★★★★★★★★☆☆ [/h2] [quote]买肯定是要买的，玩肯定是不玩的 快来关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38222893/] G胖受害者鉴赏家[/url] 让选择游戏变得更加简单[/quote] [h2]前言：[/h2] 因为本人玩过的肉鸽游戏仅有以撒系列与哈迪斯，加上本作没有中文，所以对于《Savara》我是花了一段时间来了解这个游戏后才开始游玩，接下来的一些言论多少包括一些主观思维。 [h2]玩法介绍：[/h2] 本作以上帝视角的肉鸽玩法为核心，却巧妙融合了怪猎的部位破坏与哈迪斯的爽快战斗。我在玩肉鸽游戏中经常遇到的问题就是打不过怪，好不容易拿到的一大堆道具和奖励也因为死亡惩罚而覆水东流。 但好在本作中玩家击杀怪物所收集的素材将会保留在身上，即使挑战失败也依然可以全部带回去锻造与升级武器。这种尽可能把负反馈降低的设计让我非常舒服。 战斗方面相当爽快，玩家允许从剑盾、太刀、双刀、大剑四周武器中携带两把。有类似魂游的精力槽，翻滚、攻击、冲刺都会消耗，而切换武器不仅可瞬间恢复一半精力，还可触发特殊攻击来对敌人造成伤害，像是匕首可以进行旋转位移，大锤可以打出比较高的伤害等，鼓励玩家灵活运用多武器连携。 每个怪物也有对应的武器克制，例如蘑菇弱突刺攻击，甲虫弱重武器。这点也让整个游戏在中期关卡开始变的具策略性，是采用力大砖飞的套路一把太刀配大剑一路莽到底，还是把另一把副武器换位双刀在关键时刻进行帅气位移都值得考量。 攻击时跳出来的数字金色为弱点攻击，若数字变红说明敌人的弱点被破坏（身上也会出现金色的光芒）攻击翻倍。 在精英怪身上还有类似怪猎中的部位破坏效果，像是巨大甲虫脑袋上的尖尖可以通过不断攻击来击碎。 考虑到手残玩家游戏内也配备了简单模式，看得出来制作组希望每个玩家都能够享受战斗。 [h2]缺点：[/h2] 虽然前面介绍了游戏中多种多样的武器来让玩家来进行连携战斗，但遇到精英怪和BOSS这些大体积高伤害的敌人时会很明显感觉到大部分的武器配置都不如太刀（或者剑盾）+双刀这个组合来的泛用性更强。太刀只需要在挥刀后跟随武器亮光节奏即刻进行无精力消耗的连击，在关键时刻也可以使用双刀的位移来保命，剑盾虽然有些笨重但切换后会可以挡下一次攻击。 在游戏前期吃紧的耐力管理下，无疑问太刀的推荐性更高，但恰好有些BOSS又很喜欢到处乱动时不时遮挡住角色让我无法看到太刀连击时的光点。 总结： 《Savara》是一款拥有爽快战斗的上帝视角肉鸽游戏，凭借低负反馈的成长设计（死亡保留素材）和爽快的多武器切换战斗提供了扎实的体验基础。精力条的设定鼓励玩家灵活运用武器连携，精英怪的部位破坏机制也增添了策略深度。但中后期敌人数值可能会使武器搭配过于单一，部分BOSS的视角问题也许会影响个别武器的操作流畅性。但低惩罚机制又让人觉得十分舒适，如果能进一步优化武器平衡并加上中文，肯定会更加优秀。 [h2]BUG反馈：[/h2] 若是在放弃的同时死亡，挑战失败的字样会悬挂在屏幕正上方，回到大本营后会无法和任何NPC以及商人对话，甚至可以穿过柜台和门导致无法进入战斗。需要重新开始游戏才能解决，但挑战失败的字样会保留到一轮游戏结束为止。 [quote][h3]鉴赏员测评配置：[/h3] CPU：Intel Core i9-12900K GPU：NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER 加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GgamePlayer] G胖受害者鉴赏组[/url] 和鉴赏员一起战斗！爽！ [/quote]

[h1]《Savara》We need Chinese！[/h1] 值得声明的是《Savara》即本作没有中文，但是因为只是肉鸽游戏，所以对英文水平要求并不算高，如果对本作确实是有十足的兴趣也可以随便找个翻译器一页一页翻译，总的来说有没有汉化骑士对本作实际游玩体验影响真的不算太大。 [h2]怪猎？什么时候来的？[/h2] 不得不承认，《Savara》确实有点让我震惊了，本作最具有特色的地方莫过于局外的装备打造和遗物搭配的系统，先说装备打造，它的装备打造仿纳的是怪猎那套系统，即日常战斗打小怪打boss收集素材然后合成各种模版的装备，让我比较惊讶的是除开四种武器有一堆模版+升级路线以外，装甲本身还有一堆模版可以打造，甚至在此基础之上还有套装效果，武器升级效果。 而且除开装备，技能树的升级路线采用的还是哈迪斯那套简单轻松，每一局结束都能感受到明显提升的升级树，就先不谈局内做得怎么样了，光是这个局外的升级路线就足够让玩家觉得未来可期了，只要你是喜欢玩哈迪斯的我都建议来买个玩玩。 [h2]但是话又说回来[/h2] 局外成长做得非常优秀，局内的体验呢却不是很尽人意，虽然本作一共有四种武器类型，但是每把武器的攻击方式太少了-切换武器、蓄力/普通攻击、大招，都别说跟怪猎比了，连哈迪斯都比不上，并且局内的特殊事件也基本等于0，主要的正反馈来源还是属性类型特效攻击的词条升级，但老实说那玩意充其量只是提高数值，本质攻击方式少的矛盾并没有解决。 这就导致进入战斗本身的目的不是为了战斗，而是为了去打沟槽的素材提升局外成长能力，但是好问题，提升了局外成长的能力以后我们该在那享受成长后带来的正反馈呢？没有！纯纯的本末倒置了。 [h2]这就是所谓的没有怪猎的命得了怪猎的病。[/h2] [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]
非常好玩，可以开发很多流派，就是回血道具好少啊，但武器方面建议所有切换都加上GP，不然我前中期只能双剑盾了

[h1]Short review:[/h1] It's Temu Hades. Do with that description what you want. [h1]Long review: [/h1] Honestly, the concept is not bad, but this game doesn't feel like a finished game. It feels like an early access game that got pushed out before enough depth was added. [h2] Story: [/h2] There is no story, as far as I can tell. Savara wants to be Iop's Champion and that's literally it. You have characters you talk to, but they're caricatures at best. You have "Clumsy Idiot", "Smart Guy who Reads Books", "Rival Who Hates You", and "Mentor". Those are your cast. No, they do not get any other traits. No, they do not have storylines of their own. You get a tiny bit of backstory and then 5 hours in, they have nothing else to say. If there IS more story, it's locked behind the game's Prestige system which you only unlock after defeating the final boss one time. Honestly speaking, the voice acting feels like it was wasted here. That's not to say that the VAs aren't doing their best, but I feel like they could've just not had voice acting with how little the characters ultimately matter. 1/10. [h2] Gameplay: [/h2] The basic gameplay loop is fine, but some weapons feel incompatible with others because of their movesets, and the Blessings feel like there's not much choice in what you pick. There are about 6-8 types of blessings, and unlike Hades, where you're locked into 3-4 Boon types per run after a certain point, you can see pretty much all of them in Savara. Additionally, every single effect for each boon family is on some kind of a limited-time mechanic where you either have to make as much use of them in a short span of time, they require an enemy to stay inside a specific AoE zone, or you have to constantly reposition or attack rapidly to get any use out of your boons. This would be fine if the enemies were not all more spastic than a Gen Alpha kid who's been deprived of their iPad in a busy restaurant. You honestly spend more time chasing bosses and elites around the arena than you do actually hitting them. Every boss or elite is either constantly dashing, or sitting in their own AoEs. There is so much downtime that none of your Blessings will actually get any use unless the enemy AI decides it's too overstimulated to move. It genuinely does not feel like you are the one making the choices. It feels like you are just constantly reacting to the game's choices as if none of the battle is actually in your control. Additionally, enemy hurtboxes feel incredibly inaccurate, to where you'll get regular moments of saying "That didn't hit me" when a boss clocks you for a third of your health bar. 4/10. [h2]Art: [/h2] The art style is interesting but not particularly standout. There's probably about 5 pieces of music you'll hear consistently and that's about it. 3/10. [h2] Grind: [/h2] The grind feels pretty standard for a "Monster Hunter" game, but honestly, it doesn't feel like the weapons or armor have all that much impact on your gameplay. Additionally, some parts are only obtainable from attacking elites in specific spots. This works in Monter Hunter, but not in a Roguelike where you have far less wiggle room to concentrate on specific sections of an enemy's body. Additionally, because of the above problem with enemies having way too much movement, you will constantly be chasing that particular body part just to get to what you want. 3/10. [h2] Cost vs. Enjoyment: [/h2] For $20-25, it's fine. I was at least enjoying myself at first before all the cracks started to show. If this were any higher though, I would've refunded when I could. [h2] Overall: [/h2] It feels like this game is clearly inspired from Hades. It tries to mirror a lot of the systems inherent to the game, but rather than actually being like Hades, it feels like a half-baked imitation of it. Progression feels directionless and meaningless, the story is quite literally nonexistent, and the gameplay clashes with itself at a lot of points to where it eventually just blends together and creates a frustrating swamp of barely-adequate systems. If there's more hidden under the surface, it certainly takes way too long to see it. This game should have been in early access, because as it currently stands, that's kind of how it feels. If you want a good Hades-like, just play Hades 2 when it's complete. if you want a Monster Hunter game, just go play Monster Hunter. You're not getting the best of either games here. [h1] Final Rating: 4/10. [/h1]

在Action roguelite赛道上，塞入三种物理伤害区分和抗性系统的游戏，在我目前体验过的本品类尚属于孤例。《Savara》就像是抽离了怪物猎人系列中那套迷人的对策系统，并将其转移到了一个非常lite的动作Roguelike框架中，其化学反应得到了一个体验不错且绝对独特的产物。 本作有五种武器模型，长剑，棒槌，双刀，矛，以及剑盾，他们被分配了钝击，刺击和斩击三种伤害类型。游戏中的怪物往往都能展现出对于其中一种伤害的抗性，这也是为什么本作将两把武器以及切换斩作为动作系统的核心。当你刺击一颗蘑菇怪而效果不佳的时候，最好的方法就是按q切锤给它当头一棒。这套系统无疑需要你养成条件反射般的战斗直觉，且需要在累积的战斗中，培养对于不同怪物对策的经验。好在“怪物种类少”这个一般而言的缺点，反而成为了本作优化上手曲线，快速掌握伤害系统的助力。 作为一个Roguelike游戏，《Savara》的长处完全不展现在其局内随机性上，它将可重玩性的潜力完全押注在玩家对肝出装备材料的刷子驱动，以及推进关卡的征服上。具体而言，本作的体验极大程度可定制和可预测，且你在局外就能完成大半的搭建——游戏允许你在开局时完全自定义最多30个槽位的被动天赋，以及从至多30把不同武器中选择两把。另一方面，游戏则完全没有在局内保持足够的随机性——不仅因为每种属性的祝福池十分有限，你几乎总是能在第一个boss前就点出你想走的属性路线的固定搭配；甚至你将被允许自由选择关卡Boss进行挑战。它在这些特质上确实抛弃了传统Roguelike使用不确定性下的“爽局/运营局”般的抛硬币赌局，而是让每场战斗的体验趋于可预测和均衡，没有一个build能让你跨数值地乱杀，但是积累而来的武器升级和被动可以轻易得推你走到更远，可以说放在roguelite中也lite到极致。 动作方面，本作承袭了Hades饱经验证的“技能元素强化绑定于单个动作”的成功公式，但是本作作为核心的切刀斩则为技能模式增加了更多的变数，比如以切刀为节点的增伤周期带来的双武器循环打法，成为了整个动作系统的基石。但是基于重击的Timing Hit则没有经过足够的验证，在实战中因为不能蓄力接Dash，基本在离开第一关的站桩敌人后就没有用武之地了。这种设计上的厚此薄彼究其原因还是——测试不够。 总体而言，本作画风清亮简洁却用色鲜明，在Hades基础上发展出的动作框架通过“切刀”这个伤害类型机制衔接上了怪物猎人般的怪物对策玩法，虽然为此牺牲了大量的局内随机性和构筑快感，并拉长了局外养成，但仍不失为一个优秀的动作专精的roguelike佳作。

[quote] [h1]类魂肉鸽新体验？《Savara》用“怪猎式刷装”打造你的勇士传说[/h1] 《Savara》是由[url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/Ankama]Ankama Games[/url]发行的一款动作肉鸽游戏。本作将怪猎的刷装元素和动作肉鸽类魂融在了一起，你在游戏中扮演新晋勇士萨瓦拉，你的目标很明确：收集怪物素材，打造神装，挑战各式各样的Boss，最终将自己的名字刻上荣耀殿堂。游戏目前不支持中文，可能在了解词条以及一些遗物上还是比较费力，个人推荐搭配网易的截图翻译食用。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3511456478 相比于其他类魂肉鸽游戏，本作最亮眼的莫过于它的局外成长系统。它像极了《怪物猎人》的装备打造，打怪掉素材，然后合成、升级五花八门的武器和护甲模板，甚至还有套装效果。每种武器都有自己的外观并且还能DIY颜色，武器有普攻、重击、大招以及切换攻击，但是大部分武器的招式都有点雷同（并且与怪物猎人的武器招式有点神似），作为动作游戏确实还差点意思。 不仅于此，局外还有天赋树和徽章系统，天赋树也是需要玩家在局内打怪获得素材升级解锁槽位和天赋，天赋不仅有增加基础属性的还有能够优化操作的天赋，不过天赋装备占用的槽位也有不同，有的占用1个位置，有的会占用更多；徽章给我的感觉相当于就是另类版的天赋，可以提供给你额外能力，如翻滚后提高移速等等。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3511456438 徽章需要通过和NPC对话、局内探索即可获得初版，装备上初版完成它们的升级条件即可升级，升级之后徽章提供的能力就会越强。 本作的战斗核心——伤害类型与“切刀”。游戏将武器分为钝击、刺击、斩击三种伤害类型，怪物则各有抗性。打不动？别硬刚，赶紧切换另一把武器（游戏支持双持）来针对弱点！这种“切刀斩”不仅是核心操作，更衍生出围绕切换时机的打法循环，策略性十足。怪物种类不算多，反而让玩家能更快掌握这套对策系统，算是因祸得福。不过也不是非切不可，游戏融合了肉鸽Buff元素，我就有一局用的长枪（长枪的重击是瞬发，还有一段后撤步，像极了英雄联盟里的复仇之矛），捡到了重击击中敌人落火雨，并且正好将它的冷却降低，再加上其他杂七杂八的强化重击Buff，第一关的Boss就是这样慢慢的一点点把它耗死的，不过到第二关就不见成效了，因为怪物多动加上伤害跟不上，那一句还是惜败在了狼口之下。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3511456647 在肉鸽的随机性上，本作深度比较浅，怪物种类少、随机赋能可选少，导致在局内构筑线路很少，地图内可交互元素也不多，只有一些陷阱、金币罐子以及恢复道具等等。如果你是个享受刷装过程、乐于研究装备搭配、且能接受动作相对简单的玩家，本作还是推荐一试，但若追求动作深度或丰富的局内随机事件，可能会觉得本作有点点不尽人意。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote] [/quote]

[h2] 哈迪斯+怪物猎人 [/h2] 攻击怪物，通过破坏怪物部位获得素材，用掉落的素材制作武器和装备，并进行后续升级。这是怪猎 技能分为左键普攻右键蓄力Q键切换武器以及R键特殊攻击，每个攻击键绑定一个祝福触发，不同祝福系列各有区别并可以共同发挥作用。这是哈迪斯 将怪猎和哈迪斯结合，这是本作savara 但是本作可以说完全是集合了两者的缺点，做出来的效果并不够好 作为动作肉鸽，本作没有任何能改变攻击动作的局外元素，能进行的操作比哈迪斯还要少，完全没能把握到怪猎的精髓之一：多种且独特的武器动作。敌人的ai也很简单，基本是固定的抬手+固定的出招逻辑，打起来体会不到太多的交互性。而为了让你的战斗不至于太简单，游戏使用了耐力条设定，攻击翻滚奔跑都会消耗耐力条，初始的耐力一套攻击就要见底，你只能控制好输出频率留给位移技能。另外本作除了特定动作几乎都没有霸体，移动攻击翻滚后摇前摇，只要吃到伤害就会打断动作倒地，感觉就是设计上通过这样的方式限制你的游戏进度，我个人不太喜欢这套动作逻辑。 作为roguelite，本作模仿了哈迪斯固定章节+地图+敌人的设计，下一个房间要么是祝福，要么是生命/耐力/回复道具，要么就是很大概率出现的材料/金币。在局内特意去积攒局外道具，也没有多少惊奇元素，人家哈迪斯起码还有个混沌房间有个挑战房间有个改变攻击方式的锤子呢。本作的rogue流程相对固定且重复非常严重。到后期打进阶热度的时候，会自动根据热度提升敌人数量和伤害，因为难度真的不高，只能选择堆怪来增加难度，属于找不出活的无奈之举。玩起来会有种感觉，局内在给局外打工 本作的优点，武器切换的Q比较有意思，由于武器的耐力条彼此独立，通过切换武器键Q可以后台回复耐力，且只有2scd，鼓励你不断切换武器来适应各种情景，你不喜欢也可以带两把一样的武器切换，也是ok的。武器的类型比较眼熟，片手、太刀、大剑、双刀、长枪，各类武器做出了自己的区别，怪猎玩家会见猎心喜[spoiler] 虾头太刀 [/spoiler] 综合而言，能接受大量局外，喜欢哈迪斯like，喜欢怪物猎人like，能且愿意阅读简单英语的人，[b] 以上四条全都满足推荐给你 [/b]，不然还是不推荐 +怪猎like+哈迪斯like +武器分类有点意思，初上手有新鲜感 -动作元素匮乏，武器动作少，敌人动作重复 -rogue部分依赖局外且随机性小 -盟友关系可以当做不存在，无实质影响 -后期难度设置靠增加敌人数值和堆积怪物 -无中文

[h2] 来一场真正的肉鸽大战吧[/h2] 这是一款以肉鸽作为重点的动作冒险游戏，在这里我们将成为一位勇敢的战士，受邀去参加为战神伊奥普举办的盛大庆典。然而这次庆典并非一次普通寻常的庆典，其中隐藏着巨大的阴谋正静静地等待着我们的到来。 [h2] 战斗讲究技巧[/h2] 在这里要是无脑乱打肯定是不可取的，我们要讲究策略，观察每种敌人所使用的招式，是快慢招还是远程攻击，还是只是呆板的突进袭击。及时控制身位防止被敌人包围，尝试进行逐个击破，越是进行到游戏中后期，敌人的强度和招式也会变得更加强大，特别是数量上增加。我们就要开始思考如何在敌人堆中找到突破点，这个过程十分紧张且爽快，让人肾上腺素不停地上升，当我们最终成功击败所有敌人之后，那种成就感很满足。 游戏中还隐藏着其他的战斗技巧，每名敌人的身上都有一条破防条，根据不同敌人的弱点，使用对应的武器进行攻击即可大量增长破防条，一旦破防条充满时，敌人将陷入眩晕状态，此时受到的伤害会有额外的增加，所以快速破条也是一个获胜关键。 [h2] 用敌人的东西来战斗[/h2] 天赋树的加入，为整个游戏的增加许多重复游玩的激情，我们原本可能很难才能过关的关卡，也不需要这么艰难的再次挑战才能继续探索之后的关卡。而且当我们解锁完目前可解锁的所有天赋还会有更强力的新拓展天赋等待我们解锁，多种天赋的相互配合可以产生意想不到的效果。在有些房间中我们还会被神明赐予加护，获得各种神奇的能力就像是战局内的临时天赋，在原有的基础上变得更加强大。 当然除了天赋树以外，武器防具的选择也是必不可少的，这就要本作最有特色的一个地方，那就是刷材料，所有的防具以及武器的获取，并不是通过购买解锁，而是要我们在战斗过程中击败敌人来获取到对应的材料，每种装备所需要的材料都不太相同，并且后续还有相应的升级也需要消耗大量材料。一想到这肝就有点疼，但是想想可以解锁新的装备，就感觉干劲十足。此外游戏贴心的设置了材料商店，我们也可以在其中选购自己稀缺的材料，减少一定肝度的时间。 [h2] 可优化之处[/h2] 游戏目前比较可惜的地方在于，没有较好的中文翻译，而是采用比较生硬的机翻作为中文语言包，这会出现一些武器道具的介绍不清楚，不知道这个的用途到底是什么，这会对整体游玩体验造成不小破坏。 [h2] 总结[/h2] 流畅的战斗体验，在敌人的围攻下玩出自己的一套打法，丰富的局外养成内容是重复游玩有了明确的小目标，保持玩家们高涨的游戏积极性，虽然有些不足之处，但整体是值得推荐尝试的。 [quote]关注鉴赏组[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36857896]凌动中国鉴赏协会 [/url] 加入steam组：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/5201314yongbufenli]凌动中国鉴赏协会[/url]：当'特别好评'沦为营销，我们用电竞级的较真重建鉴赏坐标系。[/quote]

[b]Pros:[/b] Runs and feels smooth to play Easy to understand harder to master type of fighting mechanics Blessings seemed well thought out Interesting badge and passive unlocks [b]Cons:[/b] Low enemy variety Low level variety (mostly mini versions of the bosses with less of same mechanics) 6 armor sets 5 weapon types (6 of each type) Only 6 bosses Mouse isn't bound to monitor even when in fullscreen? (super odd and caused quite a few unnecessary deaths) [b]Summary:[/b] Its essentially hades combined with dauntless which is an awesome concept but it should of been about 2x what it was for $20. It just needs more depth. I wasn't expecting hundreds of hours ofcourse but I was a bit surprised/disappointed when the credits rolled thinking oh...thats it??. I was expecting to beat the 6 bosses and then unlock prestige and fight another new set of harder enemies and bosses but you just reset with modifiers as "prestige" and grind the exact same enemies. levels and bosses you've been fighting and killing the whole time. Didn't see a point in grinding just to craft all the armor and weapons you never got around to crafting?? With most of the enemies just being smaller versions of the bosses with less abilities/power it gets repetitive quick. 游戏内容体量不值这个价，4小时左右基本能把所有的内容都体验到了，剩下的就是刷材料造装备升级装备，游戏打击感不错，武器方面做出了差异化，但是装备方面并没有很明显的区别，局内随机成长机制比较一般，虽然有不同的元素和类型，但是特效方面不明显。30块左右比较合适

This game has a decent base, it's literally "Hades at home", but it does the gameplay somewhat competently. The problem? There is just not enough content here. There is 3 levels. Each levels have 2 type of mobs with a couple (2 or 3) variant each. The boss at the end of the level is a elite version of these same mobs. Yes the boss fights are decent but it's nothing to write home. I managed to reach the last boss in only a couple of runs and... the game was over. I was now offered to keep playing the same handful of levels with the same handful of mobs but with some mutator to increase the difficulty, but what's the point? After 6 hours (And I probably afked for 1 hours in there), I literally don't feel the pull to ever boot the game again. The Rogue lite system is okay, like someone that successfully took note of Hades system but didn't add anything else. In fact they actually cut some content off instead. They insteaded added some meta progression system where you have to farm drops from mob to craft gears, which is nice and all (you can even recolor the gear anyway you want, which is nice), but it felt like pointless padding rather than actual game changer. The big difference between Hades and this game is the use of stamina and the stagger system ala Sekiro. It's not bad... but it feels pretty shallow. The worst part is the narration. Hades got completely carried by its story telling to the point that you'd end up continue playing just to get a bit more of these dialogues and see the story progress. Savara tried to copy that, with a handful (4) characters, but they have nothing interesting to say, deliver all dialogue too fast and in the end feel completely worthless. The sadest part is how they each seem to have clearly be designed as some kind of boss you'd have to fight at some point (each have a clear archetype, the assassin, the brawler, etc etc)... but it never happened. In the end if feels like this game needed more budget and time, it's not awful, but it feels more like a demo of a real game than a real game. Do yourself a favor and put just a tiny bit more money on the table and get Hades instead. To the devs, I wish you'll get more time and budget next time, if there is a next time, because I could see this game become a decent Hades clone, but for that won't happen without that added time and budget. This game need more levels, more enemies, better rogue lite mechanic, better narration, and more general replayability.

This is not a bad game I think it is just lacking in variety. For a roguelite there is a very small moveset, I would expect each weapon to have a unique moveset but instead each weapon "type" (and I use that loosely as some weapons look very different but are categorized the same) has a copy pasted move set leaving the combat with very little options or depth. enemies are weak to certain types of damage and its very unintuitive which weapons are strong against which enemies. enemy movesets make very little sense and are inconsistent. ending animations to attacks seem to be random and sometimes they are just skipped altogether.
I REALLY tried to love this game. But something is just lacking for me.

Fantastic game! Hades meets Monster Hunter. You're not fighting to save the world or anything grand like that, you're just a warrior fighting for glory and self-improvement and having a good time. It's refreshing to have a lighter-hearted tone for the game. Weapon variety is amazing, the effects of each weapon and each trinket have a noticeable impact and you can make some very interesting builds combined with the boons in-run. The monsters reactions to getting hit, injuring them by breaking some of their parts, and the crowd cheers feel amazing. Music and sound effects are good (especially the main menu and bossfights), voice acting is great! Slight minus if you don't know the Ankama universe as you'll miss some context and knowledge of the world and the characters, but it's still self contained, clear and fun. Difficulty is about 6/10 starting out, run modifiers can push it up quite a lot, but as you get upgrades i'd say it stabilizes at a solid 8/10 later in the game if you're pushing the challenge (note : the timer challenge mod is evil.) It's a bit short maybe, as I finished the main part of the story in about 12h, but it's well executed and not boring. Great game, no bugs, 9.5/10 would fight again.
怪猎风味的哈迪斯，再往武士刀和拳套里缝点仁王让你感受一下血压 游戏本身玩法和设计都挺好的，但是内容实在是太少了 乐趣上建议先玩哈迪斯1+2 基本上可以看做是下位代餐，也就凑合。打折可买，不值原价

An average Hades-like, slightly better than, say, Sworn. Don't expect anything new for the genre or any deep mechanics. The main problem is that all the supposed positive aspects are implemented with a significant number of flaws. The game's only major advantage is that the first few hours are spent quite well during combat. You expect the game to open up, but unfortunately, there's nothing to open up. What we have: 1) The combat is ok, but the most effective way to play is just spam. 2) The enemies and bosses are okay, but there are very few of them. 3) A large variety of weapons, which is pointless. At high ascension (/heat), the game requires speed, so the choice is dramatically reduced 4) There is little grinding, but it is overcomplicated (not excessive). 5) There are 3 types of meta-leveling, but in reality, the choice in relics and talents is almost linear. 6) There are some builds, but they are very basic (no branching paths). There is really bad build and route control. Rooms with key perks are always dual with the merchant within a run. Therefore, the in-game merchant is completely pointless. It's nonsense. Other downsides: -Overall slowness -Hitboxes -Game is easy -No plot -Visual style You'll see all the content within 6 hours. Playing it for longer than 10 doesn't make much sense. So, you have to evaluate the price-to-content ratio yourself. If you're comfortable with games like Sworn (but without co-op), give it a try, but I don't see any other target audience

The core combat is so polished and high quality that it managed to carry the game on it's own, and it makes me pretty sad this game barely got any attention. Neither the trailer nor the description really makes it clear that this is truly more of a Top down Monster Hunter rogue like, rather than your standard fast paced rogue like. I tried it on a whim and was pretty surprised by that discovery since it's so unique. Maybe that contributed to it not finding its audience, but could've also been just a bad timing... who knows when the story is so busy these days. Other than that, I would say the rogue like elements, while interesting in a vacuum, don't do enough to spice up each run. I would basically play the same way each run with maybe the sole difference being if I use my openings for basic or strong attacks. But people keep coming back to Monster Hunter for a reason, the core combat is that good. I just wish they would've embraced a bit more of the craziness of roguelikes. Modifiers changing attack animations like making hammer strong attack be a slow spin and a throw that you need to then pick up, for example. Just somethings that would make you play runs actually differently. But it is what it is, and I'm still I ended up giving this one a chance.
